note: Starting list for the task board. Live owner and status come from the claim server (waymo-api); this file is the fallback and the source of titles and details.
note_sizes: Size is S, M or L (1, 2 or 4 points); the bars count points, not tasks. Phase both = needed by either car; v1 = only the line follower (the simple alternative path); v2 = only the room scanner (the smart car for the demo). Each car's bar counts the shared work plus its own. Sizes and phases are estimates; fix them by pull request.

tasks.title: Set the three-week challenge and goals
tasks.detail: Scope and deadline are written down.

tasks.title: Pick the car's setup: local safety plus a server
tasks.detail: The ESP32 handles stopping; the server handles missions.

tasks.title: Agree on team roles
tasks.detail: Confirm who does what. One owner per active task; don't assume anyone's role.

tasks.title: Build the route simulator
tasks.detail: The browser simulator runs room missions with a stop queue.

tasks.title: Test Pause, Resume, Stop and E-stop in the simulator
tasks.detail: Automated simulator checks pass.

tasks.title: Publish the About page and team profiles
tasks.detail: Live at aintnowaymo.adsuaracloud.com.

tasks.title: Build the task board and claiming
tasks.detail: Claim and update tasks on this page or with the Discord commands (/claim, /done, /tasks).

tasks.title: Measure the diecast car
tasks.detail: Outside is 112 x 45.6 x 51.2 mm (Waymo shop, about 1:42). Use calipers for the inside: size, wheelbase, wheel size, roof height and ground clearance. Photograph the opened shell.

tasks.title: Mock-fit the ESP32, depth sensor and motor driver
tasks.detail: Check the parts fit, the camera pokes through the windshield, the turret sits on the roof, and the antenna isn't blocked by metal. Parts are candidates, not final.

tasks.title: Find where the battery, drivetrain and electronics go
tasks.detail: The donor drift car brings one drive motor, its steering and a small 1S battery. Fit them with the ESP32 and driver, and keep the battery clear of sharp metal.

tasks.title: Print the first chassis and adjust it
tasks.detail: Needs the real measurements first. Print a test fit; nothing sharp near the battery.

tasks.title: Order the donor car and motor driver
tasks.detail: The donor drift car supplies the motor, steering, wheels and battery. Confirm the fit first, then buy a small dual-channel driver (DRV8835 class) that matches the donor's motor.

tasks.title: Build the drivetrain
tasks.detail: Run the donor's motor and steering from the ESP32. Teardown (Nov 9): the steering is a small DC motor with a position pot, so the ESP32 closes the steering loop itself. Test forward, reverse, turns and slow stops. It can't turn in place, so plan wide turns.

tasks.title: Wire the battery and charging
tasks.detail: Use the donor's 1S pack (check it has its own protection board) and the XIAO's built-in charger. Check the motor starting up doesn't make the ESP32 reset.

tasks.title: Add a physical E-stop that cuts motor power
tasks.detail: Must work without Wi-Fi or the server and must not restart on its own. Do this before any self-driving test.

tasks.title: Add the chime and turn signals
tasks.detail: The chime is a must: Waymo-style tones for trip start, arrival, and a please-move tone when something blocks the car for a few seconds (same as the site's chimes). Turn signals are lowest priority. Neither may slow down obstacle checks.

tasks.title: Build the roof turret for the depth sensor
tasks.detail: Printed dome on the roof with the 2 g servo sweeping the TF-Luna lidar. Wire the servo and the lidar to the motor rail.

tasks.title: Wire the ESP32 for the car
tasks.detail: BJ, Subir and Isabel are wiring it together. Leads are soldered straight to the car's XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense with the silicone wire kit (no breadboard); the second S3 stays free for bench tests. Resistors sit inline at the pin under heat-shrink: 330 ohm per LED on D6, 100 ohm on D7 (piezo), and a 100k/100k divider on D9. DRV8833, E-stop and 470 uF cap on short soldered leads. Wire colors: black GND, red battery +, orange motor rail (after the E-stop), white 3V3, blue SDA, green SCL, yellow signals with pin-number tags. Before first power: continuity check for shorts (3V3, 5V and BAT+ against GND), then USB only. Then test that the outputs stop when commands stop.

tasks.title: Get the depth sensor working
tasks.detail: Read real distances on the ESP32-S3. The sensor sees a cone of about 60 degrees; the roof turret sweeps it to see more.

tasks.title: Add a gyro for heading
tasks.detail: A small IMU tracks heading between scans. The donor car has no wheel encoders, so distance comes from markers and scans. Measure drift over a long hallway.

tasks.title: Stop for obstacles even without Wi-Fi
tasks.detail: Stop for close objects, bad readings, lost connection or E-stop. Test with the network off.

tasks.title: Recognize room markers with the camera
tasks.detail: Start with two markers. If unsure where it is, stop instead of guessing.

tasks.title: Get the line sensor reading the tape
tasks.detail: Reflectance sensor array under the car (2 or 3 elements); tune the threshold on the real floor and tape.

tasks.title: Follow the tape and stop at the counted door
tasks.detail: Steer on the line, count door and junction marks, stop at the chosen room. No map or markers needed.

tasks.title: Place room markers (with permission)
tasks.detail: Printed markers by each door at car height so the windshield camera can read which room it is at.

tasks.title: Match the turret scan to the saved map
tasks.detail: At each stop sweep the sensor, compare the wall distances with the saved hallway, and decide where the car is. Stop if unsure. Stretch goal: fall back to gyro plus markers.

tasks.title: Set up the server for the site
tasks.detail: Container running; the app runs as a limited user.

tasks.title: Set up the MQTT broker and test the ESP32 link
tasks.detail: Bench kit ready, kept apart from the real car. Measure the delay (goal: under 150 ms for 95% of messages) and how many messages get through. Not measured yet.

tasks.title: Put the website online
tasks.detail: Live through its own Cloudflare tunnel.

tasks.title: Set up the live task board database
tasks.detail: Claims and status are saved and shared between this page and Discord. Backed up on the same machine for now.

tasks.title: Lock down the robot controls
tasks.detail: Only admins send commands; guests can only watch. Enforce it on the server, not just on the page. Keep MQTT private.

tasks.title: Connect real car data and mission history
tasks.detail: Label real, estimated and simulated data clearly. Track each command as sent, received and done. A disconnected car must not look live.

tasks.title: Auto-update the site from GitHub
tasks.detail: Merged changes go live within a minute.

tasks.title: Protect the main branch on GitHub
tasks.detail: Changes need a pull request and passing checks; no force pushes.

tasks.title: Send team updates to Discord
tasks.detail: The update form posts to Discord. Task claiming replaces it once claiming is on.

tasks.title: Check the IS building map in person
tasks.detail: The map is drawn from phone measurements. Room labels and lengths still need checking on site.

tasks.title: Measure the doors and hallway width
tasks.detail: South wall (rooms 201 to 214) is done. North wall still needed. The hand sketch wins; mark unsure doors with a guessed room number and ?.

tasks.title: Lay the tape route and junction marks (with permission)
tasks.detail: Tape line down the hallway with a mark at each door and junction so the line follower can count them. Needs permission to tape the floor.

tasks.title: Teach the car a short hallway route (scan matching)
tasks.detail: Start with two nearby rooms. Confirm the room marker on arrival.

tasks.title: Measure the north wall doors (rooms 227 to 222)
tasks.detail: Needs someone at school. Measure the wall before the first door, each door and wall width, and which doors are doubles. Then add them to the map.

tasks.title: Confirm the unclear room labels
tasks.detail: Unconfirmed: 218B, 219C, two doors both labelled 216, and a repeated 223. Check each in person. Keep guessed labels marked with a question mark until confirmed.

tasks.title: Test stopping for people and signaling
tasks.detail: Simulated only so far. Record failed tries too.

tasks.title: Drive between two rooms on its own
tasks.detail: Not done on the real car yet. Record failed tries too.

tasks.title: Test lost network and the emergency stop
tasks.detail: On the real car, supervised. Check it restarts safely afterwards.

tasks.title: Record results and prepare the SME presentation
tasks.detail: Videos, photos, delays, mission counts and failures. Tie the progress bar to finished milestones.
